exposure: causes of referral (hypertensive disorders, previous cesarean section, severe anemia)
patient socio-demographic profile (age, parity, socioeconomic background, rural/urban residence, educational status)
cohort: Obstetric patients referred from peripheral health facilities with a gestational age of 28 weeks or more.
finding: The study found that hypertensive disorders, previous cesarean section, and severe anemia were the most common indications for obstetric referrals, and maternal outcomes were largely favorable with no maternal deaths reported despite observed delays in a significant proportion of cases.
gest_age: Included patients with gestational age >=28 weeks; most referrals occurred after 36 weeks.
